plan.title: bug(hooks): agent-hook readiness probe fail-closes on a functional hook under concurrent load (fixed 1500ms budget)

narratives.Description: First-ship leftover of GitHub issue #3570. Timed-out live hook probes must not be treated as non-functional, and relief must stay under the Cursor tool.before 30s ceiling. Pair recovery copy with #3571.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`deft verify:session-ritual -- --tier=gated` fail-closes on the `agent_hooks` step whenever the machine is under concurrent load, because the readiness probe enforces a **fixed 1500ms per-hook budget** against a hook that is functionally correct. The hook exits 0 every time; it is only slower than the budget under load.

The practical effect: the gate is most likely to fail *precisely when Directive's own swarm / parallel-dispatch workflow is running*, since that workload (parallel `npm run build` / `typecheck` / test suites across several worktrees) is what pushes the hook past 1500ms.

## Measurements

Same machine, same unchanged deposit — only ambient load differs.

| Condition | `deft-hook --host claude --event tool.before` wall time | Gated ritual result |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | 0.41s, 0.49s, 0.51s, 0.56s, 0.56s | passes 3/3 |
| Parallel swarm workers active | 1.88s, then 1.36s / 1.06s / 1.20s | fails; `claude/allow`, `grok/allow`, `cursor/allow`, `codex/deny` all reported `timed-out` |

The hook itself returned **exit 0** in every one of those invocations, including the ones the probe declared timed out.

Intermediate state is also observable: after narrowing `hostHooks` to `claude` alone (one host instead of four), three consecutive gated runs on an unchanged system gave `exit 0`, `exit 1`, `exit 1` — nondeterministic, straddling the budget.

## Why this matters beyond the latency

The failure text prescribes:

> Recovery: reinstall @deftai/directive and run `deft update`

Neither addresses per-invocation latency, and `deft update` is a repo-wide rewrite rather than a narrow repair (see #3437) — so the prescribed remediation is disproportionately expensive for what is a timing budget being exceeded. An agent following the message literally performs an unplanned framework rewrite mid-task and the probe still fails.

The secondary remediation the same message offers is to disable hosts via `plan.policy.hostHooks.<host> = false`. That path has its own problem, filed separately.

## Suggested direction

Any of these would resolve the class:

- Make the per-hook budget configurable (policy field or env override) rather than a hard-coded 1500ms.
- Scale the budget to observed cold-start cost, or retry once before declaring a timeout, so a functional-but-slow hook is not reported as broken.
- Distinguish **"hook timed out"** from **"hook is non-functional"** in both the verdict and the remediation text — they are different conditions with different fixes, and only the latter warrants a reinstall.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`, tag `v0.104.0`, `managed_by: npm`, deposit `.deft/core`
- Node v22.23.2, macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
- Consumer repo: TypeScript npm workspaces; `hostHooks` currently `{claude: true, cursor: false, grok: false, codex: false}`

### Comment by @rockbox37 (2026-08-20T23:00:25Z)

Correction to the Environment section above, plus one new datapoint.

**Environment correction.** That section said `hostHooks` was `{claude: true, cursor: false, grok: false, codex: false}` on the reporting repo. That narrowing has since been **reverted** — the repo now runs the default `{claude: true, cursor: true, grok: true, codex: true}`, all four hosts registered and functional. It was reverted because the repo is worked from more than one agent host, so disabling per-host guardrails to quiet this probe was not an acceptable trade (details in #3571).

This does not weaken the report; it sharpens it. The measurements in the table were taken with all four hosts enabled, which is the configuration the probe is expected to handle, and the narrowing was only ever an attempt to work around it. **With the recommended remediation off the table, retrying is the only remaining local response to this gate** — so the fixed budget is the sole thing standing between a functional hook and a fail-closed mutation gate.

**New datapoint: the recommended remediation is also not durable.** While reverting, I removed the `hostHooks` block and ran `deft update` to regenerate. That run silently re-enabled a *different* policy field — `productSignal` came back as `enabled: true` (`source: install-force-on`) after having been explicitly disabled, because an absent key is re-force-on'd at install/update time. Only an explicit typed `false` survives. So an operator following the probe's remediation advice (edit `hostHooks`, run `deft update`) can have unrelated policy re-flipped underneath them in the same command — including outbound-telemetry policy, in a tracked file that propagates to every clone.

That interaction seems worth considering when deciding where the probe's remediation text should point, since `deft update` is currently the prescribed vehicle for both remediation paths in the failure message.

Environment (current): `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`, tag `v0.104.0`, Node v22.23.2, macOS 26.5.2 (arm64), `hostHooks` at default (all four enabled).


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T00:15:21Z)

## Triage analysis

_By: Grok 4.6 (xAI), 2026-08-20. Checked against `deftai/directive` at tag `v0.105.0` (issue bodies + comments via REST, then the live probe / deposit / policy sources)._

**Verdict:** accurate, desirable, almost ready. Lock a first-ship slice before implementing. Pair with #3571.

### Accuracy

High. The 1.5s per-fixture cap is a contract, not a guess:

- `LIVE_PROBE_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_500` in `packages/core/src/verify-env/agent-hooks-live-probe.ts`
- Same number in `content/contracts/agent-hook-readiness.md` (“each host fixture has a hard timeout of **1.5 seconds**”; four hosts × two fixtures ⇒ 12s ceiling)

`spawnSync({ timeout: 1500 })` kills the child, so the probe can report `timed-out` while a separately timed `deft-hook` still exits 0. Idle 0.4–0.6s vs loaded 1.0–1.9s is exactly the squeeze that budget has no room for. Mixed `claude/allow` / `codex/deny` failures match “stop after the first failed fixture.”

Failure copy is wrong for this class:

- live probe: `Recovery: reinstall @deftai/directive and run deft update`
- readiness wrapper: `set plan.policy.hostHooks.<host> = false, and run deft update`

Neither changes per-invocation latency. Deposit timeouts are already looser than the probe (nested hosts **5s**, Cursor `tool.before` **30s** after #3246), so the gate is stricter than the hook the host actually runs.

The body Environment line (`hostHooks` narrowed to Claude) is stale; the comment on this issue correctly restores the default all-four-hosts config, which is the configuration that was measured.

### Desirability

High. The gate fails during swarm / parallel load, which is when mutation readiness is supposed to stay green. Following the printed recovery is worse than the bug (unplanned `deft update`, or #3571 guardrail strip).

### Readiness

Almost — pick one first ship. Repro, measurements, and code anchors are enough. The body offers three directions; that is the only design fork:

1. Honest verdict: `timed-out` ≠ `non-functional`, and stop recommending reinstall / host opt-out for timeout. Cheap; should land either way.
2. One retry, or raise the budget toward the 5s nested deposit (keep a hard ceiling; 4×2×1.5s is why 1500ms exists).
3. Policy / env override — extra surface; not v1.

Recommended first ship: (1)+(2) as one story. Leave (3) out. Do not swarm this until that slice is locked.

Related: #3571 is the documented unused-host workaround this message already prints. #3437 (`deft update` as a repo-wide rewrite) is cited in the body; dry-run dest-plan work closed in 0.105.0 and does not fix this probe.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T00:27:03Z)

## Design critique of the triage comment (checked at `b6bc689a1fa50ea20ac050776723796de00d71a4`)

_By: Grok 4.5 (xAI)_

Checked against `deftai/directive` at `origin/master` tip `b6bc689a1fa50ea20ac050776723796de00d71a4` (fetched; local `HEAD` was behind). Probe/readiness/deposit sources are identical to tag `v0.105.0` on the files below (`git diff v0.105.0 origin/master --` those paths is empty). In-bounds inputs only: issue body, author comment `5363096041`, triage comment `5363616662`, plus local re-reads of the cited sources. Author wall-clock table was not re-run here (reporter: macOS arm64 under swarm load; this checkout: win32). Code/contract claims were re-measured by reading the tip blob, not by trusting line numbers from triage.

## What holds

- **Fixed 1.5s per-fixture budget is real.** `LIVE_PROBE_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_500` at `packages/core/src/verify-env/agent-hooks-live-probe.ts:13`; wired into `spawnSync({ timeout })` at `:111`. Contract text matches at `content/contracts/agent-hook-readiness.md:58` (“hard timeout of **1.5 seconds**”; four hosts × two fixtures ⇒ **12 seconds** ceiling).
- **Timeout vs process exit can diverge.** On timeout the probe records `issue: "timed-out"` (`:228–231`) from `spawnSync` `ETIMEDOUT`. A separately timed manual `deft-hook` that still exits 0 is compatible with that model; the gated ritual never sees that exit.
- **Failure copy is wrong for this class.** Live probe failure message always ends with `Recovery: reinstall @deftai/directive and run \`deft update\`` (`:323`) for every case class, including `timed-out`. Readiness wrapper appends hostHooks opt-out + `deft update` on any live failure (`agent-hook-readiness.ts:229`). Neither path changes per-invocation latency.
- **Deposit budgets are looser than the probe.** Nested Claude/Grok/Codex deposit timeout `NESTED_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5` (`init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts:55`); Cursor `tool.before` deposit `CURSOR_TOOL_BEFORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30` after #3246 (`:52`, comment block immediately above documents the ~12s readiness ceiling). Gate is stricter than the host-facing budgets.
- **Per-host stop-after-first-fixture is real.** Fixture loop `break` at `agent-hooks-live-probe.ts:303`; host status collapses any case failure (including timeout) to `non-functional` at `:306`. The probe still continues across remaining hosts, which matches a multi-host `claude/allow` / `…` / `codex/deny` summary under load.
- **Triage framing is right on desirability and “almost ready.”** Swarm/parallel load is exactly when mutation readiness is supposed to stay green; printed recovery steers into collateral (#3571 / broad `deft update`). Author follow-up correctly retires narrowed-hostHooks as an acceptable workaround.
- **Propose-not-apply posture is correct.** Lock a first-ship slice before code.

## Findings

1. **[blocks-the-design]** First-ship option (2) as written (“raise the budget toward the 5s nested deposit”) is unsafe without a simultaneous ceiling rewrite. At four enabled hosts × two fixtures, 5s/case ⇒ **40s** absolute ceiling. Cursor deposit stays **30s** and was raised specifically so host `failClosed` does not kill a ritual that re-runs live readiness (#3246 comment at `agent-hooks.ts:43–51`; contract ceiling still **12s** at `agent-hook-readiness.md:58`). A naive 1500→5000 raise re-opens the #3246 class unless Cursor timeout and the contract ceiling move in the same story. Prefer: **one retry at 1.5s** (worst case 24s < 30s) **or** a modest raise that keeps `hosts × fixtures × budget ≤ ~20–24s`, with contract + Cursor deposit updated if the ceiling moves.

2. **[blocks-the-design]** “Honest verdict” is not free text alone. `timed-out` already exists as a case `issue` (`:18`, `:230`), but readiness maps every live failure to `functionality/liveStatus = non-functional` (`agent-hook-readiness.ts:204–216`) and always prints reinstall/hostHooks recovery. First ship must branch remediation (and preferably the readiness dimension / message) on `timed-out` vs missing/drift/bad-envelope. Leaving the enum while still saying “non-functional → reinstall” fails the class the issue names.

3. **[sharpens-framing]** “Stop after the first failed fixture” in triage should be stated as **per host**, not as whole-probe early exit. Code continues the outer host loop after a per-host `break` (`:290–306`). That is what makes all-four-hosts timeout reports possible in one gated run.

4. **[sharpens-framing]** Author comment `5363096041` adds a durability point triage under-weights for recovery design: following printed `deft update` can re-force-on unrelated policy (`productSignal` cited). Pair recovery rewrite with “do not prescribe `deft update` for timeout”; #3437 / #3571 are not optional footnotes for copy work.

5. **[footnote]** No policy/env knob for `LIVE_PROBE_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS` exists under `packages/types` / `packages/core/src/policy` (search at tip: no hits). Triage’s deferral of configurable override to post-v1 is consistent with inventory.

6. **[footnote]** Maintainer source checkouts skip the live gate (`agent-hook-readiness.ts:159–168`). This bug class is consumer/deposit-path; tip re-verification here is structural, not a local ritual fail reproduction.

## Existing mechanisms

Do not invent a new readiness subsystem. Extend what already exists:

| Mechanism | Role now | Fit for #3570 |
|---|---|---|
| `LIVE_PROBE_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS` + contract “Probe budget” | Hard per-fixture cap + 12s ceiling | Adjust carefully; ceiling is load-bearing for #3246 |
| Case `issue: "timed-out"` | Already distinguished in probe cases | Branch message / readiness mapping on it |
| `hostHooks` policy | Intentional unused-host opt-out | Keep; stop advertising it as timeout recovery |
| `NESTED_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (5s) | Host deposit budget for nested hooks | Upper reference only; not a free probe target |
| `CURSOR_TOOL_BEFORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30s) | Host budget covering readiness ceiling | Hard constraint on any probe raise/retry product |
| Gated `agent_hooks` → `verify:hooks-installed --scope=agent --live` | Non-deferrable mutation gate | Keep fail-closed; fix what “closed” means |
| Test seam `spawnHook` / timeout unit test (`agent-hooks-live-probe.test.ts` ~310–318) | Deterministic timeout path | Extend for retry + remediation-branch tests |

## Injection / swarm lens

Hostile or headless envelopes that spawn parallel builds/tests are the ambient load that pushes hooks past 1.5s. Fail-closed then blocks the next mutation ceremony **because** Directive is working hard — the worst time to print “reinstall / `deft update` / disable hostHooks.” An agent that obeys the message mid-swarm performs an unplanned framework rewrite or strips guardrails (#3571), and may still see timeout. Raising the probe blindly until Cursor’s 30s host kill fires converts a flaky readiness failure into an opaque host `exit-1` with no Directive allow/deny (#3246 recurrence). Retry-once or a ceiling-aware modest raise preserves fail-closed against broken hooks without teaching agents to dismantle policy under load.

## Road not taken

**Policy/env override as v1** (body direction 3; triage deferred): loses because it adds operator surface and still needs a safe default under swarm load; does not fix wrong remediation for the default path.

**Copy-only ship with no retry/budget change:** loses because measurements already show idle passes and load straddles 1.5s; honest text without relief leaves the gate red during the workflow the framework itself creates.

**Raise every case to 5s without touching Cursor/contract ceilings:** loses — see finding 1; trades one false-red for host failClosed kills.

**Load-detect / skip live probe when busy:** loses thin fail-closed (#3265) — softens the gate instead of making timeout a distinct, remediable condition.

Winner for first ship: **(1) timeout-specific verdict + remediation** plus **(2a) one retry or a modest raise that keeps multi-host ceiling under the Cursor 30s deposit**, with contract text updated in the same change if the ceiling moves. Leave configurable override out.

## Score against Directive rules

| Rule | Score |
|---|---|
| Authority ladder | **Pass** — triage cites contract + probe/readiness sources rather than issue prose alone. |
| Fail-closed | **Mixed** — gate correctly fail-closes on bad hooks; currently also fail-closes on “slow but exit-0 under load,” which is the bug. |
| Propose-not-apply | **Pass** — triage refuses implement-before-slice-lock. |
| Claim-cites-state (#2066) | **Pass on code**; author Environment line was correctly marked stale vs comment `5363096041`. |
| Gate integrity (#3156) | **At risk if first ship is “disable host / skip probe / raise past Cursor budget.”** Fix the product condition and remediation; do not green the gate by gutting it. |
| Thin fail-closed (#3265) | **Fail today** — one check, but remediation is not the matching one for `timed-out`. First ship restores “one check + one *correct* remediation.” |

## Disposition

**Uphold** the triage’s diagnosis and desirability. **Amend** the recommended first ship before any implement dispatch:

1. Branch probe/readiness messaging (and preferably readiness mapping) so `timed-out` ≠ “reinstall / hostHooks=false.”
2. Add **one retry** and/or a **ceiling-aware** budget change; **do not** treat “raise toward 5s” as unconstrained.
3. If the absolute ceiling moves, update `content/contracts/agent-hook-readiness.md` and keep `CURSOR_TOOL_BEFORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` strictly above that ceiling in the same story.
4. Keep configurable policy override out of v1.
5. Pair with #3571 for the unused-host workaround story; do not use host opt-out as the timeout fix.

Ready for a locked scope xBRIEF after that slice text is explicit — not before.
